The Lions need Jared Goff protected long enough to let Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs turn short completions into field-flipping gains, while avoiding stalled drives against a Saints defense eager to test the new system. New Orleans, meanwhile, must protect its quarterback and manufacture explosive plays without living in obvious passing situations, because Detroit's rush can turn long-yardage downs into a game-changing problem.

2026_01_NYJ_TEN.headline: Can Tennessee force the Jets to win the long way?
2026_01_NYJ_TEN.paragraph1: The Jets need their revamped offense to manufacture explosive gains before Tennessee can turn the game into a slog. That puts pressure on Aaron Glenn’s group to protect the quarterback, create space for Breece Hall if available, and punish a Titans defense adjusting to Gus Bradley. Tennessee’s answer is to stay efficient on early downs with Cam Ward, then avoid obvious passing situations where New York’s rush can attack a vulnerable protection unit. 2026_01_WAS_PHI.headline: Philadelphia’s Front Wins the Battle for Jayden Daniels’ Playbook
